## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), the associated rectangle is \(i^j\), with \(i=s-t+1\) and \(j=r-t+1\). [source-2, lines 1354-1362]
- [source-backed] The nonidentity bigrassmannians are parameterized by \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\), and \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) is explicitly the permutation in lines 987–991. [source-2, lines 973-992]
- [proved] Put \(q=n-r\). The inverse correspondence is
  \[
  t=r-j+1,\qquad s=i+r-j,\qquad n=r+q.
  \]
  The source admissibility conditions are equivalent to
  \[
  1\le i\le q,\qquad1\le j\le r.
  \]
  Indeed, admissibility gives \(i,j\ge1\), \(j\le r\), and
  \(t>r+s-n\iff q-i+1>0\iff i\le q\). Conversely, these rectangle bounds give \(1\le t\le r\), \(t\le s<n\), and \(t-(r+s-n)=q-i+1>0\).
- [proved] This correspondence is injective: from \((r,s,t,n)\), recover \((q,i,j)=(n-r,s-t+1,r-t+1)\); from \((r,q,i,j)\), recover \((r,s,t,n)\) by the preceding inverse formulas.
- [source-backed] Each prescribed generating family has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements, where \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-2, lines 1382-1421]
- [proved] For nonempty rectangles, \(\binom{a+b}{a}>1\) exactly when
  \[
  1\le i\le q-1,\qquad1\le j\le r-1.
  \]
- [proved] Under the convention
  \[
  \{r\le5,\ q\le6\}\setminus\{r\le4,\ q\le5\},
  \]
  the 90 deduplicated bigrassmannian instances with \(\binom{a+b}{a}>1\) are
  \[
  v_{5,\,i+5-j,\,6-j,\,q+5},
  \quad 2\le q\le6,\ 1\le i\le q-1,\ 1\le j\le4,
  \]
  giving \(4(1+2+3+4+5)=60\) cases, together with
  \[
  v_{r,\,i+r-j,\,r-j+1,\,r+6},
  \quad 2\le r\le4,\ 1\le i\le5,\ 1\le j\le r-1,
  \]
  giving \(5(1+2+3)=30\) cases. The two families are disjoint since their \(r\)-values are respectively \(5\) and \(2,3,4\); injectivity proves there are no further duplicates.
- [source-backed] The paper reports computer verification of minimality only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2, lines 1495-1502]

## Strategy
Use the sourced rectangle correspondence, prove its inverse admissible, then apply the established \(N>1\) criterion and substitute \(s=i+r-j,\ t=r-j+1,\ n=r+q\).

## Gaps
The boundary-expansion convention is not source-stated. Minimality for the 90 translated cases remains unproved.

## Next
Independently review the inversion and finite enumeration; then test selected translated cases for minimality.
